title: Content consumption and browsing calibration: prespecified evaluation plan

global_rules.fit_on: train split only; every candidate and baseline sees exactly the same train rows
global_rules.selection: the candidate (baselines included) with the best primary metric on the validation split is selected; ties within 1e-4 go to the simpler candidate
global_rules.confirmation: on the test split the selected candidate's primary metric is compared with the best simple baseline's; if a baseline is strictly better on test the baseline is kept and the report says why the learned model failed
global_rules.worse_model_kept: never: the kept model's primary test metric must be no worse than every simple baseline's
global_rules.test_once: test metrics are computed after selection and no candidate is refitted after test metrics are seen
global_rules.uncertainty: user-cluster bootstrap, 200 resamples, seed 0: 95% interval of the kept model's primary test metric and of its difference from the best baseline
global_rules.user_split: bucket = int(sha256('e1:' + str(user_id)).hexdigest()[:8], 16) % 100; train 0-69, validation 70-84, test 85-99 (KuaiRand); MIND train-file users: fit 0-79, validation 80-99
global_rules.ece: expected calibration error with 15 equal-width probability bins, weighted by bin size
global_rules.auc: ROC AUC (Mann-Whitney) on the pooled split; for MIND also the mean AUC over impressions with at least one click and one non-click
global_rules.missing_data: KuaiRand rows with duration_ms <= 0 take video_duration from video_features_basic; rows still without a positive duration are dropped and counted; MIND empty histories give zero text affinity and category shares equal to the prior; news without abstract use the title only
global_rules.leakage: all history features use only events strictly before the row's day (KuaiRand) or hour (MIND); the KuaiRand video_features_statistic file is not used because its aggregates are not time-stamped and include the test period

hyperparameters.logistic: L2-regularised logistic regression on standardised features, C = 1.0, lbfgs, max_iter 1000
hyperparameters.gbdt: HistGradientBoostingClassifier(learning_rate=0.05, max_iter=400, max_leaf_nodes=31, min_samples_leaf=200, l2_regularization=1.0, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.1, n_iter_no_change=20, random_state=0)
hyperparameters.quantile_linear: monotone quantile network without hidden layer, Adam lr 3e-3, batch 4096, at most 25 epochs, early stopping on validation pinball loss (patience 3), seed 0
hyperparameters.quantile_mlp: monotone quantile network with two tanh hidden layers of 32 units, same optimiser and stopping rule
hyperparameters.gamma_poisson: maximum marginal likelihood of the negative-binomial (gamma-Poisson) model with scipy L-BFGS-B

content_consumption.estimand: P(an individual consumes (keeps watching, is_click = 1) a video shown in the single-column featured feed (tab 1) | exposure, features), under exposure NOT selected on unobserved preferences
content_consumption.rows: tab 1 rows of the random-exposure log (is_rand = 1)

splits.train: random-exposure rows of train users dated 2022-04-22..2022-05-02
splits.validation: random-exposure rows of validation users dated 2022-04-29..2022-05-02
splits.test: random-exposure rows of test users dated 2022-05-03..2022-05-08 (held-out users and later time)

candidates.B1_popularity: logistic on item_click_rate and item_log_pop_7d only (simple baseline: the 4.0-style popularity rule)
candidates.O_logistic: logistic fitted on the observational standard-log train split (transported to random exposure)
candidates.O_gbdt: GBDT fitted on the observational standard-log train split (transported)
candidates.O_gbdt_recalibrated: O_gbdt plus one intercept offset fitted on the random-exposure train split
candidates.R_logistic: logistic fitted on the random-exposure train split
candidates.R_gbdt: GBDT fitted on the random-exposure train split

extra_reports: observational model on all random-exposure rows of test users 04-22..05-08
coefficient comparison of logistic models fitted on observational vs random-exposure rows
repeat-consumption rate and the effect of item_played_before

content_consumption_feed.estimand: P(consume | the production recommender exposed the video in the featured feed, features): an observational engagement predictor, which includes the recommender's selection on preferences the features do not capture
content_consumption_feed.rows: tab 1 rows of the standard logs

splits.train: standard-log rows of train users dated 2022-04-12..2022-05-02
splits.validation: standard-log rows of validation users dated 2022-04-29..2022-05-02
splits.test: standard-log rows of test users dated 2022-05-03..2022-05-08
splits.test_time_only: standard-log rows of train users dated 2022-05-03..2022-05-08 (reported, not used for selection)
splits.transport_random: random-exposure rows of test users dated 2022-04-22..2022-05-08 (how the observational fit fares under random exposure)

watch_duration.estimand: conditional distribution of y = log1p(play_time_s) for a feed exposure, given whether the video was consumed (is_click), its duration and affinity features
watch_duration.rows: tab 1 rows of the standard and random-exposure logs pooled

splits.train: rows of train users dated 2022-04-12..2022-05-02 (standard) and 2022-04-22..2022-05-02 (random)
splits.test: rows of test users dated 2022-05-03..2022-05-08; reported pooled, per log (standard / random) and per branch (consumed / skipped)

candidates.B0_unconditional: empirical quantiles of y on train (simple baseline)
candidates.B1_duration_bins: empirical quantiles of y per decile of duration crossed with consumed (simple baseline)

watch_duration.distribution_checks: per duration decile and per branch: observed vs sampled watch-time quantiles, completion rate (watch >= duration) and view rate (watch >= min(30 s, 50% of duration))

return_daily.estimand: P(an individual is active (has at least one logged feed exposure) on day d | activity history before d)
return_daily.rows: user-days 2022-04-29..2022-05-08 of all 27,285 users; activity from the standard and random-exposure logs

candidates.B1_own_rate: (active_days_7d + 1) / 9, the individual's own smoothed recent rate (rule baseline, no fitting)

return_daily.distribution_checks: forward simulation of the 4 test days per test user from the model (simulated activity fed back into the features), 20 draws: distribution of the number of active days (total variation distance to observed) and the retention curve of users active on 2022-05-04

session_rate.estimand: heterogeneity across individuals of the number of extra sessions per active day (sessions - 1; a session ends after a 30-minute gap)

splits.train: train users, active days 2022-04-22..2022-05-04 (fit of the population distribution)
splits.test: test users: counts on 2022-04-22..2022-05-04 predict the rate on 2022-05-05..2022-05-08

candidates.B1_own_mean: the individual's own raw mean in the history window
candidates.M1_gamma_poisson: gamma-Poisson: posterior mean rate per individual

session_rate.validation_note: B0/B1/M1 have at most two population parameters; selection uses the train-user forward split (history 04-22..04-30 -> rate 05-01..05-04) as validation

news_click.estimand: P(click | news shown in an impression, the user's click history, the news text, category, popularity and age)

splits.train: train-file impressions of fit users dated 2019-11-10..2019-11-13, 50,000 impressions sampled with seed 0 (2019-11-09 is warm-up for popularity and first-seen times)
splits.validation: train-file impressions of validation users dated 2019-11-14
splits.test: all dev-file impressions (2019-11-15: later day; 88% of them from users absent from the train file); reported overall and for users absent from the train file

news_click.text_representation: TF-IDF (sublinear tf, English stop words, min_df 3, at most 50,000 terms) of title + abstract fitted on train-file news, reduced to 128 dimensions by truncated SVD (seed 0) and L2-normalised; the user profile is the normalised mean of the history vectors
